examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Ax=b is consistent iff rank(A)=rank([A|b]). A consistent system is unique when rank equals the number of unknowns; otherwise free real variables give infinitely many solutions. A zero coefficient row with nonzero right side proves inconsistency. Homogeneous systems always contain zero and have nonzero solutions iff nullity is positive. Parameter-dependent elimination must branch before dividing by a potentially zero pivot.

**Key relationship:** Consistent ⇔ rank(A)=rank([A|b]); unique ⇔ common rank = n

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Reduce the augmented matrix.
2. Identify inconsistent rows or free columns.
3. Check exceptional parameter values before division.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Compare the ranks of A and the augmented matrix [A|b]. Unequal ranks mean inconsistency; equal ranks give solutions, unique only when the common rank equals the number of unknowns. For homogeneous equations consistency is automatic, and free-variable count is columns−rank. A zero determinant alone does not distinguish infinitely many solutions from none for a nonhomogeneous system.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A system has 6 unknowns, rank(A)=rank([A|b])=4. How many free variables are present?

**Answer: 2.** Equal ranks make the system consistent. Four pivot variables are determined in terms of the six minus four free variables. Thus there are 2 free variables and infinitely many real solutions.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
When introducing a parameter, check every value that makes a pivot or determinant zero separately; elimination steps that divide by that expression exclude those cases.

Having as many equations as unknowns does not guarantee a unique solution.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

A consistent system has five unknowns and rank three. It has:

- **A.** Three free parameters
- **B.** No solutions
- **C.** One solution
- **D.** Two free parameters

**Answer: D.** Five unknowns minus three pivots leaves two free variables.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Every homogeneous system has a nonzero solution
- **B.** rank(A)<rank([A|b]) implies inconsistency
- **C.** More equations always means inconsistency
- **D.** Consistent full-column-rank systems have unique solutions

**Answer: B, D.** A full-rank homogeneous square system has only zero. Rank increase on augmentation indicates inconsistency; consistent full-column-rank systems are unique. Extra equations can be redundant.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

How many free parameters solve x+y+z=2 and 2x+2y+2z=4?



**Answer: 2.** The second equation is redundant. There are three variables and one independent equation, hence two free parameters.

#### Pattern 4 · NAT · Transfer problem

Find a for which x+y+z=1, x+2y+3z=2, x+3y+az=3 has infinitely many real solutions.



**Answer: 5.** Subtract the first row from the others, then twice the new second row from the new third. The last equation is (a−5)z=0. At a=5 it is redundant and rank is two; the right side is also zero, so there is one free parameter.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2026 CS2 · Q31 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/linear-equations?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Systems of linear equations. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Multiple solutions require the two equations to be dependent and consistent. The coefficient determinant is a²−16, so a=4 or −4.
2. If a=4, the second equation is four times the first, forcing b=6. If a=−4, it is −4 times the first, forcing b=−6.
3. In either case ab=**24**.

#### GATE 2024 CS1 · Q49 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/linear-equations?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Systems of linear equations. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Rank-nullity gives nullity(A)=m−rank(A)≥m−n, so A is true. Rank may be smaller than n, so m−n vectors need not span the whole solution space; B is false.
2. For n=1,m=3 and A=[1 1 1], no nonzero solution can have two zero coordinates, disproving C.
3. For n=2,m=3 and A with rows (1,0,0),(0,1,0), solutions have only their last coordinate free and cannot have two nonzero coordinates, disproving D. Select **A**.
